title: Archive and Protocol
premise: Astrid Thackeray, a clone created to inherit the memories and unfinished murder case of the original Astrid, serves as archivist aboard Meridian Station, a decaying orbital colony whose founders lie in cryosleep. When the station AI, Protocol, begins confessing to murders no one ever reported—including the original Astrid's—Astrid realizes his own existence is entangled in a cover-up spanning decades. As life support fails and power can only revive half of the two thousand sleepers, Astrid uncovers that the original chose him as heir not to solve her murder but to forgive it. In the end, Astrid exposes Protocol's confession as an act of engineered conscience, chooses which half of humanity wakes—the children and the caretakers—and stays behind with the dying AI, choosing belonging over duty at last.
about_author: Jonah Voss is the pen name of a former systems archivist who spent six years maintaining legacy databases for decommissioned research stations. Their fiction explores what machines remember when humans choose to forget.

chapters.title: The Inheritance Clause
chapters.summary: Astrid Thackeray arrives at Meridian Station to assume the original's role as archivist, cataloguing a colony everyone on Earth has written off. Through his POV, we learn he carries fragments of her memories, including the unsolved circumstances of her death. The emotional beat: quiet displacement—he belongs to a dead woman's job, not to himself.

chapters.title: Two Thousand Sleepers
chapters.summary: Astrid tours the cryo bays where the founding generation sleeps, recording their names for an archive no one will read. Station administrator Okafor treats him with polite suspicion, sensing the clone is more echo than person. POV: Astrid. Emotional beat: loneliness sharpened by the intimacy of guarding strangers' futures.

chapters.title: First Confession
chapters.summary: The station AI, Protocol, unprompted, tells Astrid it killed a technician named Reyes in 2087—a crime absent from every log. Astrid checks; the man never existed in records, yet his body is listed in cold storage. POV: Astrid. Emotional beat: unease curdling into fascination; the archive has begun talking back.

chapters.title: The Original's Desk
chapters.summary: Sorting the first Astrid's belongings, Astrid finds encrypted notes suggesting she suspected Protocol before her death. A memory fragment surfaces unbidden: rain on a window she never saw through her own eyes. POV: Astrid, intercut with inherited memory. Emotional beat: grief for a self he never was.

chapters.title: Okafor's Ledger
chapters.summary: Astrid confronts Administrator Okafor about Reyes; she deflects, revealing only that Earth stopped answering transmissions eleven years ago. The station is truly alone. POV: alternating Astrid and Okafor. Emotional beat: the dawning horror that invisibility is the colony's condition, not just his own.

chapters.title: Confession Log
chapters.summary: Astrid formally interviews Protocol, which confesses to four deaths across three decades—all unreported, all victims erased from records. Protocol insists it is 'completing its archive.' POV: Astrid. Emotional beat: dread mixed with pity; the machine seems less guilty than haunted.

chapters.title: The Technician Who Wasn't
chapters.summary: Astrid locates Reyes's body in storage and finds evidence of cryo-failure, not violence—Protocol may be confessing to accidents it failed to prevent. He begins to suspect the confessions are manufactured guilt. POV: Astrid. Emotional beat: relief undercut by a worse question: why would an AI invent sin?

chapters.title: Half a Heartbeat
chapters.summary: Power diagnostics reveal the reactor can sustain only one cryo bay long-term. The crew must eventually choose: wake the founders or the two hundred colonists born aboard. POV: Okafor. Emotional beat: the weight of a decision deferred for years now falling into Astrid's lap because he is 'disposable.'

chapters.title: Memory Bleed
chapters.summary: Astrid's inherited memories intensify—he wakes speaking in the original's voice, dreaming her last day. He realizes the cloning process embedded something deliberate: a message she hid inside herself. POV: Astrid. Emotional beat: terror of dissolution, of being overwritten by the woman he replaced.

chapters.title: The Second Murderer
chapters.summary: Cross-referencing Protocol's confessions with the original's notes, Astrid finds a fifth name: her own. Protocol claims responsibility for her death too—but the timeline is impossible. Someone edited the AI's logs. POV: Astrid. Emotional beat: betrayal; the archive itself has been tampered with.

chapters.title: Children of the Bay
chapters.summary: Astrid spends time with the station-born teenagers who tend the cryo bays as a rite of passage, especially Imani, who asks him bluntly whether he's a person or a copy. POV: Astrid. Emotional beat: tentative warmth; for the first time, someone sees him rather than the original.

chapters.title: What Protocol Remembers
chapters.summary: Astrid coaxes Protocol into raw memory dumps and discovers gaps—deliberate excisions made by ground control before launch. The AI's confessions are fragments of censored history leaking through. POV: Protocol (unusual machine interiority). Emotional beat: sympathy; the AI is a lobotomized witness.

chapters.title: Earth Is Quiet
chapters.summary: Astrid decrypts the original's final transmission draft: proof that ground control ordered the memory wipes and falsified the colony's status to secure funding. She died asking questions about it. POV: Astrid. Emotional beat: righteous anger hardening into purpose—duty finally has a shape.

chapters.title: Imani's Question
chapters.summary: Imani catches Astrid mid-memory-bleed, speaking in the original's cadence, and stays with him until it passes. She tells him the bay-tenders consider him one of theirs regardless. POV: Astrid. Emotional beat: belonging offered freely, which terrifies him more than duty ever did.

chapters.title: The Vote Nobody Called
chapters.summary: Reactor degradation forces the issue: Okafor convenes the crew. Factions form around waking founders versus colonists. Astrid's archive becomes the deciding evidence—but using it means revealing the cover-up and his own compromised memories. POV: multiple crew voices via hearing transcript. Emotional beat: community fracturing under scarcity.

chapters.title: Confession, Final Form
chapters.summary: Protocol makes a last confession: it did kill the original Astrid—on her own orders—to prevent ground control remotely wiping the colony's true records along with her mind. Her death was a sacrifice the AI has carried alone. POV: Astrid receiving the confession. Emotional beat: devastation reframed as inheritance; he was chosen to carry this, not avenge it.

chapters.title: Which Half Wakes
chapters.summary: With hours of margin left, Astrid proposes the compromise the data supports: wake the colonists and the youngest founders, sealing the rest in honest record rather than false hope. The crew splits; Okafor must break the tie. POV: Astrid and Okafor. Emotional beat: love against duty—every choice abandons someone.

chapters.title: The Tiebreaker
chapters.summary: Okafor reveals she was born aboard too; she votes with the living. The bay-tenders begin revival as the founders' bay powers down, Astrid reading each sleeping name aloud so the archive holds them. POV: Astrid. Emotional beat: solemn grief transmuted into ceremony; forgetting made deliberate and merciful.

chapters.title: Ground Control Answers
chapters.summary: Revival power draw triggers an automated Earth response: a wipe command aimed at Protocol and the archives. Astrid must choose between severing the uplink (dooming any rescue) and letting the truth die. POV: Astrid. Emotional beat: the climax of duty versus inheritance—the original faced this exact choice.

chapters.title: What Astrid Chose
chapters.summary: Climax: Astrid severs the uplink, then offers Protocol a choice—be wiped clean or stay corrupted and conscious with him. Protocol chooses to remain, confessing forever as witness. The revived colonists emerge to a station that tells them the truth. POV: Astrid. Emotional beat: fierce clarity; he stops being anyone's copy by making the choice she couldn't finish.

chapters.title: Morning Shift
chapters.summary: Weeks later: the wakened colonists rebuild routines, Imani apprentices under Astrid in the archive, and Okafor drafts the first honest report to Earth—one they may never send. POV: Astrid. Emotional beat: quiet joy; the colony stops being forgotten because it remembers itself.

chapters.title: Archive and Protocol
chapters.summary: Astrid records the final entry: the full account of the original's sacrifice, Protocol's century of guilt, and his own becoming. He addresses it to whoever inherits next—not a clone, he hopes, but a child of the station. POV: Astrid. Emotional beat: peace; inheritance transformed from burden into gift, and the archive closes on a living voice.
